shared.name: Choice identifier key
shared.source: reading 104: https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#DataCharacteristic_SimpleChoice.Attr_identifier (§5.132.1, and §5.7.1, §5.55.1, §5.56.1, §5.58.1, §5.65.1, §5.67.1, §5.73.1 and §5.131.1: 'This identifier must not be used by any other choice or item variable', five classes naming their own noun) and https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#Derived_Identifier (§7.16: an identifier is 'a logical reference to another object in the item, such as an itemVariable or choice'); reading 104 as amended: each class's sentence bars its own noun ('any other gap', 'text', 'image', 'hotspot', 'hottext choice'), so no two elements of one class share an identifier, and the four classes' 'any other choice' bars every element the information model calls a choice (§6.17 GapChoice, §5.59, §5.65.1), a gap none (§5.57, gaps filled 'from an associated set of choices'), so a simple, inline, hotspot or simple associable choice shares its identifier with no other choice or hottext of its document, whichever interactions hold them, nor with one its assembly places, compared collapsed; a gap and a gap text may share one (interactions.ts key(on(Choice, "document", "kind", "identifier")), key(on(Hottext, "document", "identifier")) and their placed keys, and queries.ts key(on(ChoiceSpaceName, "document", "identifier")) and key(on(PlacedChoiceSpaceName, "assembly", "identifier")))

They are completionStatus, numAttempts and duration'), each spelled exactly, with no alias, the identifier compared collapsed (references.ts BuiltInVariable, its session variables); reading 168: a test's processing holds duration and neither of the other two (§2.2.2, reading 29), so an item's declaration names none of the three and a test's declaration only duration, and a test's own numAttempts and completionStatus shadow no built-in and are accepted (declarations.ts itemSessionVariables and testSessionVariables, by the declaration's parent kind); the context variable QTI_CONTEXT is Reserved type's

shared.name: Typed attribute value
shared.source: readings 7 and 8, and https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#Enumerated_BaseTypeEnum (§8.14, BaseTypeEnum, each base type's value set): a qti-map-entry's map-key is a value of its mapping's base type (§7.21.1, 'The source value'), and a lookup table entry's target-value and a table's default-value are values of its outcome's base type (§5.90.1, §5.78.1, §7.23.2, §7.18.3); each is its base type's lexical form, read as written for string and, for every other base type, after XML Schema's collapse, the whiteSpace facet every typed simple type fixes (https://www.w3.org/TR/xmlschema-2/#rf-whiteSpace, §4.3.6: 'whiteSpace is applicable to all atomic and list datatypes ... For all atomic datatypes other than string (and types derived by restriction from it) the value of whiteSpace is collapse'), so ' 3 ' is the integer 3 (reading 7; mapping.ts Typed_attribute_value over expression-types.ts BaseTypePattern)

shared.name: MappableBaseType

entry.name: Weight key
entry.source: https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#DerivedCharacteristic_Weight.Attr_identifier (§7.50.1: 'An item can have any number of weights, each one is given an identifier that is used to refer to the weight in outcomes processing') and §7.47.2 ('The weight identifier refers to a weight definition in the corresponding qti-assessment-item-ref'), with reading 74's reasoning: one identifier written twice under one item ref would name two weights, and a weight-identifier that names it could not tell which, so no two weights of one item ref share an identifier, compared collapsed (overlay-queries/tests.ts WeightName)

shared.name: Mastery range
shared.source: reading 9: the Schematron's RULE SPECIFIC CLASS OUTCOMEDEC 1 (ASI 3.0.1 XSD, on qti-outcome-declaration: 'not(@mastery-value < @normal-minimum)', 'The mastery-value attribute value must not be less than the normal-minimum value'; 'not(@mastery-value > @normal-maximum)', 'The mastery-value attribute value must not be greater than the normal-maximum value'), read by its intent: each pair judged where both have a value, a normal-minimum an outcome declaration does not write being its XSD default 0.0 (reading 149), as xs:double values, each form collapsed as xs:double's whiteSpace collapses it (XML Schema Part 2 §4.3.6; reading 7) and, where it is in xs:double's lexical space (XML Schema 1.0's, reading 71's edition, operators.ts doublePattern), read as the double XML Schema 1.1's doubleLexicalMap maps it to (Part 2 §3.3.5.2, reading 144; grizzle's Text.parseDouble), of any digits and any exponent, NaN ordered against nothing (declarations.ts doublesInOrder)

entry.source: reading 2: https://www.w3.org/TR/MathML3/chapter3.html#presm.maction (MathML 3 §3.7.1.1: 'If the value specified is out of range, it is an error' and 'If no selected sub-expression exists, it is a MathML error'): an maction has at least one element child and its selection, 1 when absent, is at most their number

entry.source: https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#DataCharacteristic_TextEntryInteraction.Attr_pattern-mask (§5.162.5, and §5.48.4 of ExtendedTextInteraction: 'If given, the pattern-mask specifies a regular expression that the candidate's response must match in order to be considered valid. The regular expression language used is defined in Appendix F of [XSCHEMA, 01].') and https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#DataCharacteristic_PatternMatch.Attr_pattern (§5.104.1: 'The syntax for the regular expression language is as defined in Appendix F of [XSCHEMA, 01].'), the information model narrowing the XSD's xs:string: every pattern-mask, and every pattern of a qti-pattern-match that names no variable in braces (a StringOrVariableRef's literal), is a string of XML Schema 1.0 Part 2 Appendix F's regExp production, { and } metacharacters (reading 58), judged by grizzle's Xml.isPattern (overlay-queries/interaction.ts PatternText)

shared.name: Test name key
shared.source: reading 86: https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#RootCharacteristic_AssessmentSection.Attr_identifier (§4.2.1: 'The identifier of the section or item reference must be unique within the test and must not be the identifier of any testPart'), §5.159.1 and §7.5.3 ('A test may refer to the same section multiple times within a test. Note however that each reference must have a unique identifier'), read over the assembled test (reading 5): the test document and every document its section refs and includes place; a section document placed twice is one document and names nothing twice: no two written test parts, sections, section refs or item refs of one test's assembly share an identifier (overlay-queries/tests.ts AssembledName)

entry.name: default hotspot last slot
entry.source: reading 80: https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#DataAttribute_HotspotInteraction_qti-hotspot-choice (§5.68.6, and the HotspotChoice class description, §5.67: 'The default hotspot, if defined, must appear last'), of qti-hotspot-choice only, since the AssociableHotspot class (§5.7) and the graphic associate interaction's hotspots (§5.59.4) state no such rule; last among its parent's element children, so whitespace, comments and instructions after it do not count (children.ts LastWhere, ruling D3)

shared.name: Value cardinality
shared.source: https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#Enumerated_CardinalityEnum (§8.17, CardinalityEnum: single 'a single value'; record 'a set of independent values each identified by its own identifier and having its own base-type') and https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#Derived_Value (§7.46.1, §7.46.2: field-identifier and base-type are 'only used for' a value that forms part of a record): a single variable's default or correct value holds one qti-value, and every value of a record's default or correct value is a field, with its field-identifier and base-type both (§8.16, record: 'a set of independent values each identified by its own identifier and having its own base-type'); a value of any other variable may write either attribute, which names and types nothing there (§7.46: 'The base-type is defined by the 'base-type' attribute of the declaration except in the case of variables with record cardinality'), so none is refused for it (overlay-queries/declaration.ts RecordSetValue)

shared.name: Template default target
shared.source: the UP audit's A37 and reading 108: https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#DataCharacteristic_TemplateDefault.Attr_template-identifier (§5.152.1: 'The identifier of the template variable affected'; §5.152: 'The default value of a template variable in an item can be overridden based on the test context'): a template default's item ref names an item, and the default names a template declaration of that item, compared collapsed (overlay-queries/tests.ts TemplateDefault, ItemTemplateDefault); an item ref that names an LTI link names no item, so a template default under it is refused (reading 110); one whose href lies outside the package names an item the package does not hold, and its template default is stored unchecked (SV-LAW-02)

shared.name: Outcome only
shared.source: https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#AbstractAttribute_ExpressionGroup_qti-number-correct (§6.9.58 to §6.9.64 and §6.9.41, normative: qti-number-correct, qti-number-incorrect, qti-number-presented, qti-number-responded, qti-number-selected, qti-outcome-minimum, qti-outcome-maximum and qti-test-variables, each 'which can only be used in outcomes processing'); and a qti-variable that writes weight-identifier, https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#DerivedCharacteristic_Variable.Attr_weight-identifier (§7.47.2: 'Weights are defined only in the test context (and hence only in outcomes processing)'; spec reading 199) (expressions.ts Outcome_only, its language Processing's; queries.ts Outcome only over WeightedVariable; the old checker's P25)

shared.name: Printed variable type
shared.source: reading 234: https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#Union_IntegerOrVariableRef (§9.3.3, IntegerOrVariableRef, normative: 'The type used for attributes of integer type that may be replaced with the value of a template or outcome variable of base type integer and single cardinality'), the type of a printed variable's base and index (https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#DerivedCharacteristic_PrintedVariable.Attr_base, §7.30.8 and §7.30.9): a base or index that names a declared variable names a single integer one, its cardinality and its base type each judged where the declaration spells one (readings 158 and 159), an item's own against its declarations and a fragment's per placement against its assembly's (reading 117); a check over the queries PrintedIntegerCardinality and PrintedIntegerBaseType (queries.ts)

shared.source: IMS Content Packaging 1.2: a listed document is an entry of the package, and one document: a resource names the document at its href, read as a document of its type (reading 93), so no path is listed as documents of two types (qti/package.ts, Document's key over package and path)

entry.name: Branch target
entry.source: reading 87: https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#Data_BranchRule (§5.23: 'In the case of an item or section, the target must refer to an item or section in the same test-part that has not yet been presented. For test-parts, the target must refer to another test-part'; §5.23.1, the reserved EXIT_SECTION, EXIT_TESTPART and EXIT_TEST) and https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#Data_Ordering (§5.98: 'It is therefore an error to make such an item the target of a branch-rule', of an item a selection with replacement can repeat): a target is an exit, or names a test part from a test part's rule, or an item ref or section of the source's own test part from an item ref's or a section's rule, never an item ref under a selection with replacement, read over the assembled test from the rule's placement: its own instance and the instances that hold it, a section ref the leaf of its placement (§7.5: 'branching rules should treat referred sections as leaf nodes'), and the root of a fragment an include places a target there too, its part and order not judged, a recorded under-refusal (overlay-queries/tests.ts TargetedBranchRule, ResolvedBranchRule)

shared.name: Arity
shared.source: https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#Abstract_ExpressionGroup (§6.9, ExpressionGroup: each operator's attribute is of a container class whose logic attribute's multiplicity is its sub-expression count, §5.83.1 Logic0toMany '[0.. unbounded]', §5.84.1 Logic1toMany and §5.94.1 NumericLogic1toMany '[1.. unbounded]', §5.85.1 LogicPair '[2]' and §5.86.1 LogicSingle '[1]', or of its own class, whose logic attribute states its count, as §5.113.2 Repeat's '[1.. unbounded]' with §5.113's 'The repeat operator takes one or more sub-expressions', over §6.9.49's '0 or more'; a leaf class's children row reads 'There are no children.'; as §6.9.21, https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#AbstractAttribute_ExpressionGroup_qti-match, 'The match operator takes two sub-expressions') (expression.ts OperatorArity); reading 21; and reading 242, https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#Data_MathOperator (§5.91, MathOperator: 'The trigonometric functions, sin, cos and tan, take one argument in radians ... Other functions take one numerical argument. Further functions might take more than one numerical argument, e.g. atan2 (two argument arc tan)'; §8.25, MathOperatorNameEnum: 'atan2 - the 2-argument inverse trigonometric tangent obtained from the two arguments', every other token a function of 'the argument'): a math operator named atan2 holds exactly two sub-expressions and one of any other name exactly one (overlay-queries/expression.ts MathOperand, BinaryMathOperator)

shared.name: Reserved type
shared.source: https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#RootAttribute_AssessmentItem_qti-context-declaration (§4.1.10, and §4.4.7 of a test: 'An implementation MUST support the global variable "QTI_CONTEXT" with record cardinality') and https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#Data_ContextDeclaration (§5.34: 'There is one built-in context variable named "QTI_CONTEXT" with record cardinality'), which the implementation guide, a document with no normative mark, declares explicitly (its §3.7.11, 'an explicit (though unnecessary) <qti-context-declaration> of QTI_CONTEXT'): a declaration of QTI_CONTEXT is a record context declaration, since one of another kind or cardinality would make one identifier name two variables (reading 74). SCORE, MAXSCORE and PASSED are typed by no normative rule: §4.5's 'SCORE needs to be a float', 'MAXSCORE needs to be a float' and 'PASSED needs to be a boolean' use no RFC 2119 keyword (§1.3 Conventions), §2.2.2.3's 'MUST' is in a section marked NOT NORMATIVE, and no XSD particle or Schematron rule types them, so a declaration of any type is admitted (J1; the lead's ruling, 2026-11-20)

shared.name: Key text bound
shared.source: src/qti/limits.ts: no index orders by a name, a prefix or a path (the host orders them), and each bound on a text a query reads is PostgreSQL's: a text a query reads by a pattern (matchedText) at most matchedTextBytes UTF-8 bytes, the regex engine's (regexTextMaxBytes); a foreign element's namespace name and local name at most foreignNameBytes each, half of what that engine reads of the expanded name a query matches them as (OpenElementName.expanded), since XML puts no bound on a name (reading 94); and an ARIA bound of a pair that is an xs:decimal at most parsedDecimalBytes, what Text.parseDecimal reads (decimalTextMaxBytes), past which a decimal may name a value numeric does not hold (overlay-queries/interaction.ts Key_text_bound over AriaBounds); a stated limit of the representation, not a law of the specification

entry.source: reading 122: https://www.imsglobal.org/sites/default/files/spec/qti/v3/md-bind/index.html (QTI 3.0 Metadata §2.7.5.1, Learning Resource Type: 'the LOM-defined values self assessment and exam are forbidden', normative by its §1.2): a learningResourceType of the LOM vocabulary holds neither, its term the LOM vocabulary's where its source is LOMv1.0, empty, or not written, which the loose binding defaults to LOMv1.0 (imsmd_loose_v1p3p2.xsd:1288); a term of another source is another vocabulary's, which the loose binding does not enforce (§3.6), and is not refused; source and value compared collapsed (queries.ts ForbiddenResourceType contained in OtherVocabularyType, over the learning resource type's folded lom:value and lom:source)

entry.source: reading 81: https://www.w3.org/TR/xmlschema-1/#cvc-wildcard (XML Schema 1.0 Part 1 §3.10.4, Item Valid (Wildcard), clause 2: a strict wildcard's element has the context-determined declaration mustFind), with §3.3.4 clause 1.2 and §3.3.5 [validity] clause 1.1.3: an element only the strict wildcards of its parent's model hold (install.ts StrictlyHeld) stands only under an xsi:type naming a type of its document's schema set or a built-in, so it has a governing type, its OpenElementType row (C44; shred: strict-undeclared), but for reading 6's root whose declaration the wildcard finds (§3.10.4 clause 2, §3.3.4 clause 1.1.1.3.2), kept foreign and unrefused (install.ts HeldRootsUnder, C13)

shared.source: reading 75: https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#Data_ResponseDeclaration (§5.115: 'Response variables are declared by response declarations and bound to interactions in the itemBody'), https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#DataCharacteristic_BasePromptInteraction.Attr_response-identifier (§5.15.7, and §5.18.6, §5.19.6, §5.45.1 and §5.162.1, each of multiplicity [1]: 'The response variable associated with the interaction') and each interaction class's binding sentence, as https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#Data_ChoiceInteraction (§5.30: 'The ChoiceInteraction must be bound to a response variable with a base-type of identifier and single or multiple cardinality'): an interaction's response-identifier names a response declaration of its item; the text entry interaction's response-identifier is the XSD's IDREF (reading 14), every other interaction's, the extended text interaction's among them, an IdentifierDType this law resolves

entry.source: https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#DataAttribute_ResponseCondition_qti-response-if (§5.114.1, and §5.114.2 and §5.117 of the response branches, §5.99.1, §5.99.2 and §5.101 of the outcome branches, and §5.149.1, §5.149.2 and §5.154 of the template branches: each 'consists of an expression which must have an effective base-type of boolean and single cardinality'), and https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#Data_TemplateConstraint (§5.150: 'A templateConstraint contains an expression which must have an effective base-type of boolean and single cardinality') (expressions.ts Condition_type; the old checker's P21); a located response processing template's rules run as its item's own (https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#Root_ResponseProcessing, §4.6.1 template: 'The rules obtained from the external template may be used instead of the rules defined within the item itself, though if both are given the internal rules are still preferred'; §4.6.2 template-location: 'an alternative URI, typically a relative URI to be resolved relative to the location of the qti-assessment-item itself, that can be used to obtain a copy of the response processing template'), so its references are judged among the item's declarations and its expressions typed in the item, as reading 117 judges an included fragment's (names.ts LocatedTemplate; overlay-queries/expression.ts placedDocuments, PlacedExpressionNode)

entry.name: MathML align placement
entry.source: reading 2: https://www.w3.org/TR/MathML3/chapter3.html#presm.malign.group (MathML 3 §3.5.5.2: an maligngroup in a table cell stands in the cell directly or inside an mrow or mstyle that changes no direction, mphantom, mfenced, the selected sub-expression of an maction, or semantics) and #presm.malign.mtable (§3.5.5.9); a group with no cell above it is ignored, only an maction's selected sub-expression is checked, and a change of direction is a dir other than the one the element inherits, so mrow dir='ltr' in a formula that reads left to right changes none (operator decision 321); m:math inherits none, since 'the dir attribute defaults to "ltr" on the math element' (MathML 3 §2.2.1, reading 164)

entry.source: reading 87: https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#Data_BranchRule (§5.23: 'the test jumps forward to the item, section or part referred to by the target identifier', 'the target must refer to an item or section in the same test-part that has not yet been presented'), §2.8.3.2 ('cycles are not allowed') and §5.98 (the child elements of an invisible section not kept together 'are mixed into the parent's selection prior to shuffling'): a target starts after its source's end, so it is neither the source, nor an ancestor, nor a descendant of it, unless the two are apart and the section nearest above both reorders its children, a shuffling section or one an invisible section not kept together mixes into; fixed is not read, a recorded limit (overlay-queries/tests.ts ForwardBranchRule)
